title: Xanthe and the Harvest
premise: Urban explorer Yara Thornbury descends into unmapped tunnels beneath the dying village of Hollowmere, where a church bell that was melted down in 1911 still rings, summoning the descendants of the founding families to an old covenant: every harvest moon, the village must 'count' its people and give up one to the thing in the tunnels, or it takes them all. Yara, a Thornbury by blood they never knew, is pulled into the count alongside the last family of Hollowmere. To survive, Yara must help the family flee before the harvest moon rises — but the tunnels only let out what the bell allows, and escape demands someone stay behind to answer the roll call. In the end, Yara tricks the counting thing with a recorded voice and a stolen name, buying the family their freedom at the cost of their own certainty about who they are.
about_author: Felix Crane is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping decommissioned mine shafts across northern England before turning to horror fiction. They write in the margins of old ordnance maps and claim never to explore alone anymore.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't Cast
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Mapping storm drains beneath Hollowmere, Yara finds a tunnel absent from every survey and hears a bell toll overhead — though records say the church bell was melted down in 1911. Emerging, they find villagers frozen mid-step, all facing the churchyard. The emotional beat is skeptical curiosity curdling into dread as Yara realizes the sound came from below.

chapters.title: The Counting House
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, alternating with matriarch Edith Vale's journal entries. The Vales, Hollowmere's last founding family, take Yara in and reveal the covenant: each harvest moon the thing beneath counts the bloodlines, and shortfalls are paid in full. Yara discovers the name 'Thornbury' on the ledger — their own. The beat is reluctant belonging; for the first time, Yara has a family, and it comes with a debt.

chapters.title: What the Tunnels Allow
chapters.summary: The family attempts to flee before moonrise, but every road loops back to Hollowmere and the tunnels reshape behind them. Yara realizes the bell doesn't summon the thing — it summons the counted, and Yara's blood makes escape impossible for everyone. The climax builds as Edith prepares to sacrifice herself, and Yara, refusing to be saved again, steals the ledger and descends alone. Beat: love weaponized against duty.

chapters.title: Answer When Called
chapters.summary: Yara's POV in the dark beneath the church. Facing the counting thing — a patient, many-mouthed absence wearing melted bell-brass — Yara plays a recording of Edith's voice answering the roll while striking the dead bell's clapper to mask the lie. The count passes; the family walks out at dawn. But Yara stays a moment too long, and something now answers to their name whenever bells ring anywhere. Beat: survival won, innocence spent.
